Town in Ulster County · ZIP 12401, 12484 · Population 5,600

Back to Ulster County

Why Marbletown Businesses Choose Direct Mail

The Town of Marbletown encompasses the hamlets of Stone Ridge, High Falls, and Cottekill in the agricultural and arts-rich interior of Ulster County. Stone Ridge in particular has emerged as a meaningful dining and hospitality destination — the Kitchen Table restaurant, Hasbrouck House hotel, and Stone Ridge Orchard draw regular visitors from New York City and across the Hudson Valley, creating a weekend tourism economy that coexists with the town's long-established agricultural and homeowner base.

Stone Ridge sits along Route 209 between Kingston and Ellenville; High Falls is set on the D&H Canal towpath where the Rondout Creek drops through a dramatic stone gorge — a scenic draw that sustains the hamlet's restaurant and arts economy.

Local Market Profile: Marbletown

Marbletown's population is spread across three hamlets with different commercial profiles. Stone Ridge (ZIP 12484) is the most commercially active, anchored by the growing restaurant and hospitality scene along Route 209 and a concentration of antique shops and specialty retail. High Falls (ZIP 12440) is a scenic D&H Canal hamlet built around a dramatic Rondout Creek gorge, with upscale restaurants and the High Falls Food Co-op as anchors. Cottekill (ZIP 12419) is the smallest and most rural — a quiet hamlet adjacent to Rosendale with little commercial activity of its own. All three hamlets share an affluent, arts-oriented demographic with strong engagement with quality print materials.

EDDM Strategy for Marbletown

Marbletown's hamlets span three ZIP codes (12484, 12440, 12419), which means a full-town EDDM campaign requires coordinating three separate postal entries or working with a mailer that handles multi-ZIP drops as a unified project. Each hamlet's carrier route footprint is small enough that individual hamlet campaigns are affordable — Stone Ridge's 12484 EDDM runs an estimated $600–$900 for core residential routes. Cornerstone manages multi-hamlet drops under a single project at no additional complexity cost to the client.

The Town of Marbletown has roughly 6,000 residents across its three hamlets, with a demographic skewed toward homeowners, second-home buyers, and retirees — a high-value direct mail audience with above-average discretionary and home maintenance spending.

Marbletown Direct Mail FAQ

Can I combine Stone Ridge and High Falls in one EDDM campaign?

Stone Ridge (12484) and High Falls (12440) are separate ZIP codes requiring separate postal entries for EDDM, but Cornerstone handles both as a single project — one proof approval, one production run, coordinated drop dates. The combined footprint of both hamlets is small enough to be affordable at an estimated $900–$1,400 all-in, depending on route selection. We provide household counts per route before you commit.

How do Stone Ridge restaurants and hotels reach the NYC weekend visitor audience?

EDDM reaches local Marbletown residents, not the weekend visitors driving up from the city. For Stone Ridge's tourism dining and hospitality audience, targeted mailing lists filtered by households in NYC, Brooklyn, Westchester, and Rockland County with dining and travel interest indicators are more effective. Many Stone Ridge restaurants and hotels run dual campaigns: local EDDM for the resident market and targeted list mailings for the NYC visitor audience, timed to coordinate delivery for maximum seasonal impact.
